numerical_failure.observed_behavior: In scipy 1.14.0, scipy.special.pro_rad1(1,1,30,1.1) returns (-93126.77064342781, 2390688.1114633614), and the reporter says results are wrong for all input parameters tried.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: pro_rad1(1,1,30,1.1) should return (0.009657798960703628, 3.253343602674869), matching scipy 1.11.4, which the issue reporter says agrees with Mathematica (SpheroidalS1 gives 0.00965787 and its prime gives 3.25337).
trigger_conditions: the wrong values trace to sphj in specfun being mistranslated from Fortran (argument order and dj indexing)
oracle_clues: scipy 1.11.4 output used as the correct reference

numerical_characteristics.tolerance: rtol=2e-5 in the added test_pro_rad1; PR body states rtol 1e-5 for the added test; commit message mentions bumping test tolerance for linux 32bit
category_specific_evidence: Issue #21058: scipy 1.14.0 pro_rad1(1,1,30,1.1) returns (-93126.77064342781, 2390688.1114633614), while scipy 1.11.4 returns (0.009657798960703628, 3.253343602674869), which agrees with Mathematica SpheroidalS1 and SpheroidalS1Prime values 0.00965787 and 3.25337
Added test reference values from WolframAlpha: SpheroidalS1(1, 1, 30, 1.1) = 0.009657872296166435 and SpheroidalS1Prime(1, 1, 30, 1.1) = 3.253369651472877
Root cause per discussion: sphj dj array is zero-indexed in Fortran, so the n=0 branch should write dj[1] = 1.0/3.0 instead of dj[0]
PR #21062 states sphj was mistranslated from Fortran to C++ and is only used by pro_rad1; the existing test did not cover the affected cases
Commit 'Fix sphj argument order' and 'Fix indices in sphj' accompany the fix; a diff in msta2 returning nn + 10 is a perturbation shown in passages, not part of the fix
reproduction_risks: The msta2 diff changes return value to nn + 10, which would itself corrupt results; it should not be treated as the fix
Test tolerance is relatively loose (rtol 1e-5 to 2e-5) and the commit notes a 32-bit Linux tolerance bump, so exact matching may fail on some platforms
Reproducer prints version via scipy.__version__; the installed version used for the reference output is not otherwise specified
Mathematica output in the issue is given to only about 6 significant digits
